title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - operation metadata foundations
description: The declared contract characteristics of one operation: its scope, side effects, and job/pagination/idempotency/precondition/audit posture. This document defines the shape a future per-operation catalogue entry will carry; it registers no operations of its own, since the operation payload catalogue is a later phase. This document declares no root type; it is a definition container only.

OperationSideEffect.title: OperationSideEffect
OperationSideEffect.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming whether invoking an operation mutates state, such as `none` or `create` or `update` or `delete`. Open by design so a compatible minor release can add classifications without breaking existing decoders.

OperationScopeKind.title: OperationScopeKind
OperationScopeKind.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming the kind of scope an operation carries, such as `installation` or `workspace`. Open by design so a compatible minor release can add scope kinds without breaking existing decoders. A given operation's scope metadata carries exactly one kind.

OperationScope.title: OperationScope
OperationScope.description: What an operation itself declares it needs and touches, independent of any single caller's request.

required_scopes.description: Scopes a caller must hold to invoke this operation.

side_effect.description: Whether invoking this operation mutates state.

scope_kind.description: The single scope kind this operation requires, such as `installation` or `workspace`.

OperationCompletionMode.title: OperationCompletionMode
OperationCompletionMode.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming how an operation completes, such as `synchronous` (no durable job, ever), `may_return_job` (a response may carry a `JobReference`), or `always_returns_job` (every invocation starts a durable job). Independent of `OperationSideEffect`: an operation like `import.start` is representable as a mutation (`side_effect`) that always returns a durable job (`completion_mode`). Open by design so a compatible minor release can add modes without breaking existing decoders.

OperationJobMetadata.title: OperationJobMetadata
OperationJobMetadata.description: How an operation completes and, when durable work is involved, what kind of job it starts.

completion_mode.description: How this operation completes: synchronously, optionally through a job, or always through a job.

job_kind.description: Open code naming the kind of job this operation starts, when `completion_mode` entails one.

terminal_result_schema_ref.description: Reference to the JSON Schema governing `JobTerminalSuccess.result` for the job this operation starts. This is what makes terminal success typed rather than opaque: `result_kind` names the shape and this reference resolves it. Absent until the operation catalogue binds it, in which case the binding is a semantic rule rather than a published reference.

OperationPaginationMetadata.title: OperationPaginationMetadata
OperationPaginationMetadata.description: Whether and how an operation's results are paginated.

paginated.description: Whether this operation's result may span more than one page.

max_page_size.description: Largest page size this operation accepts, when paginated.

OperationIdempotencyMetadata.title: OperationIdempotencyMetadata
OperationIdempotencyMetadata.description: How this operation may safely be retried. The three fields are not independent: `required` entails `supports_idempotency_key` (an operation cannot demand a key it does not honour), `safe_to_retry` excludes `required` (a request that is safe to repeat without a key cannot also be rejected for lacking one), and an operation that does not support keys cannot require them. A combination breaking any of those is a metadata statement no implementation can satisfy.

required.description: Whether omitting the idempotency key is itself rejected. A mutation that starts durable work or changes a job's control state requires one, so a network-level repeat can never become a second mutation; omitting it is a non-retryable invalid request, not a silently accepted single-shot call.

safe_to_retry.description: Whether an identical request may be retried without an idempotency key, such as a plain read.

OperationPreconditionMetadata.title: OperationPreconditionMetadata
OperationPreconditionMetadata.description: How this operation uses optimistic-concurrency preconditions.

required.description: Whether omitting the precondition is itself rejected for this mutation.

OperationAuditMetadata.title: OperationAuditMetadata
OperationAuditMetadata.description: Whether and how this operation is audited.

audited.description: Whether invoking this operation produces an audit record.

audit_category.description: Open code categorizing this operation's audit records, when audited.

SchemaReference.title: SchemaReference
SchemaReference.description: A URI reference to the JSON Schema document governing an operation's input or result payload.

OperationMetadata.title: OperationMetadata
OperationMetadata.description: The full declared contract characteristics of one operation: its scope, payload schemas, required capability, side effects, and job/pagination/idempotency/precondition/audit/error posture. This is the complete shape a future per-operation catalogue entry will carry, so publishing that catalogue is additive rather than requiring later required-field breaks. Binding this to a concrete request/result payload and publishing a catalogue of operations is out of scope for this document.

scope.description: What this operation requires and touches.

input_schema_ref.description: Reference to the JSON Schema governing this operation's `input` payload.

result_schema_ref.description: Reference to the JSON Schema governing this operation's `result` payload.

required_capability.description: The capability, and minimum version, this operation depends on.

job.description: How this operation completes and whether it may return asynchronous work.

pagination.description: Whether and how this operation's results are paginated.

idempotency.description: How this operation may safely be retried.

precondition.description: How this operation uses optimistic-concurrency preconditions.

audit.description: Whether and how this operation is audited.

allowed_errors.description: The stable error codes this operation may fail with.
